extracted.intended_audience: microbiologists and bacterial taxonomists preparing or publishing prokaryote names
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for naming prokaryotic taxa (valid publication, types, minimal descriptions, approved lists, deposition of type strains, and related procedures under the International Code of Nomenclature of Prokaryotes/earlier Bacteriological Code).

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid publication (IJSB requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: New names and combinations must be published in the International Journal of Systematic Bacteriology (IJSB) or, if published previously elsewhere, an announcement of such publication must be made in the IJSB; a description or a reference to a previously and effectively published description of the named taxon must also be given in the IJSB and the type of a named taxon must be designated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All new names are validly published only in the IJSB, although they may be effectively published elsewhere and then validated by announcement in Validation Lists in the IJSB. For valid publication, nomenclatural types must be designated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting date and Approved Lists (1 January 1980)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new starting date (1 January 1980) was proposed so that valid publication requirements could be made more meaningful; for names published prior to this date, Approved Lists of Bacterial Names were compiled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Names not on those Approved Lists lost their standing in nomenclature, which cleared away many obsolete names. Old names not on the lists remain available for revival individually if the specific provisions for revival are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement on Approved Lists: adequacy and types required
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the names of bacteria which are adequately described and for which there is a type or neotype strain, if the organism is cultivable, will be placed on the Approved Lists of Bacterial Names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compilation of Approved Lists is done by taxonomic subcommittees and other experts for approval by the Judicial Commission and the ICSB; omission from the Approved Lists means loss of standing unless revived according to the Code's provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and definition of Type (Type Culture)
rubrics_metrics.description: The type of a named taxon must be designated; the growing recognition of the value of the type concept may mean incorporation into the Code of a definition of Type Culture in stabilization of bacteriological nomenclature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type designation is a requirement for valid publication; for cultivable organisms the Code recommends deposition of type strains in culture collections to ensure availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal standards for taxon descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICSB requests its taxonomic subcommittees and other experts to propose lists of characteristics which will constitute the minimal standards for the description of various taxa; the Code recommends that the description of each named taxon contain at least those characteristics specified in the minimal standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These minimal-characteristic lists are to be approved by the ICSB; the recommendation is that descriptions include at least those characteristics and thereby provide clear, precise applications of names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposition of type strains in culture collections
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of cultivable organisms, cultures of the type strains of newly named species and subspecies should be deposited in culture collections from which they would be available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositing type strains in accessible collections is recommended to support reproducibility, verification and stability of names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of names published outside IJSB (Validation Lists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Names effectively published elsewhere may be validated by announcement in Validation Lists in the IJSB to achieve valid publication under the Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors publishing new names outside IJSB must ensure an announcement and sufficient description/reference appears in the IJSB (Validation Lists) so the name attains valid status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conserved and Rejected Names; Opinions of the Judicial Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code includes Lists of Conserved and Rejected Names of Bacterial Taxa together with Opinions issued by the Judicial Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Judicial Commission issues Opinions and adjudicates nomenclatural disputes; Appendix and Statutes describe procedures for Requests for Opinions and administration of these lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of Requests for Opinions (procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a prescribed procedure (appendix) for preparation of a Request for an Opinion to the Judicial Commission when nomenclatural issues need formal adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors or committees should follow the Appendix guidance when preparing submissions requesting the Judicial Commission's opinion; the Code and appendices include examples and editorial notes on such requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthography rules and illustrative examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix 9 addresses orthography and the Code includes examples (and in some cases hypothetical examples) to illustrate orthographic rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where bacteriological examples were not available, hypothetical or botanical examples were sometimes used; Appendix 9 contains orthography guidance and examples to prevent misleading usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infrasubspecific subdivisions and caution against confusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The increasing use of terminologies applicable to strains and groups of bacteria of infrasubspecific rank makes necessary careful study of the best methods for preventing confusion, even some degree of nomenclatural chaos, in the naming of taxa of lower rank than subspecies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix 10 treats infrasubspecific subdivisions; the Code signals the need for rules or recommendations to manage lower-rank naming practices to avoid instability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional status 'Candidatus' (appropriate application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix 11 addresses the appropriate application of the Candidatus concept for provisional status of taxa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of the Candidatus designation is governed by the Appendix guidance to indicate provisional standing when organisms cannot meet full requirements (e.g., not cultivated); authors should apply the concept per the Code's recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of examples to illustrate clauses when bacteriological cases lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples have been included in the Code where they were thought helpful to illustrate clauses, but in a few instances examples from bacteriology have not so far been found; in those cases hypothetical examples or those taken from botany were used (noted particularly for orthography).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers and authors should treat hypothetical or borrowed examples as illustrative only and follow the Code's text and appendices for substantive rule application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Statutes and administrative rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The volume includes the Statutes of the International Committee on Systematic Bacteriology (ICSB) and Statutes dealing with administration of the ICSB and related bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative provisions govern how the Code is managed, how lists and Opinions are compiled/issued, and how committees operate; authors and committees should consult statutes for procedural compliance.
